title: Perfectness is preserved by coefficient duality
statement: In the Poincare duality conventions [def-pod-conventions], with $X$ and coefficient stage $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ as fixed there, let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] be perfect over $\Lambda_X$ [def-pod-perfect-complex-on-x]. Then its coefficient dual $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\Lambda_X)$ [def-pod-coefficient-dual-on-x], formed with the coefficient-stage derived internal Hom [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], is perfect over $\Lambda_X$ as well, and $K^\vee\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$.

proof.text: Use the coefficient-stage units and operations of [def-pod-coefficient-dual-on-x] and [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and put $H=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\Lambda_X)$. First check its constructible domain. The constant coefficient object theorem [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible] puts $\Lambda_X$ in $D^b_c$ at each stage, and identifies every finite reduction of the completed integral unit with $(A_{E,j})_X[0]$. At a finite stage, tensoring the unit with any module sheaf in degree zero is that sheaf, so its Tor interval is $[0,0]$. The same calculation for all integral reductions gives the uniform interval $[0,0]$. At either field stage $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Hence $\Lambda_X$ and the given $K$ both lie in $D^b_{ctf}$. Apply [thm-sf-ctf-stability] (ii) to these two inputs at finite coefficients. At integral coefficients apply its clause (vii), which states $D^b_c=D^b_{ctf}$ and preservation by internal Hom; the same clause transports preservation to $E$ and the common finite-stage $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ category. Thus $H\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ in every case. Here $X$ is separated of finite type over $k$ and $\ell\ne p$ by the fixed Poincare conventions; no properness, ambient exceptional adjoint, dimension-free Hom bound, or additional six-functor axiom is used.

source.place: Final sentence (constructible finite-Tor conclusion), expanded using main-20261015 thm-sf-ctf-stability, clauses (ii) and (vii).

proof.text: For finite or integral coefficients put respectively $R=(A_{E,n})_X$ or $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$. By [def-pod-perfect-complex-on-x] and [def-weil-site-perfect-complex], on a cover of every object of the small pro-etale site there is a bounded representative $P^\bullet$ for $K$, with $P^r=0$ outside some $[a,b]$, each $P^r$ a direct summand of $R^{\oplus m_r}$. Bounds and ranks may depend on the covering object. Restriction of module sheaves is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] identifies $H|_U$ with $R\mathcal Hom_{R|_U}(K|_U,R|_U)$. The integral internal Hom is the ambient ringed-site Hom over the completed sheaf, as specified in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Consequently it suffices to calculate this Hom for $P$ on each such slice; discrete constant $\mathcal O_E$-sheaves are never substituted for the completed unit.

Write the degreewise splitting as $P^r\xrightarrow{i_r}R^{\oplus m_r}\xrightarrow{p_r}P^r$ with $p_ri_r=1$. Precomposition gives $\mathcal Hom_R(P^r,R)\xrightarrow{p_r^*}\mathcal Hom_R(R^{\oplus m_r},R)\xrightarrow{i_r^*}\mathcal Hom_R(P^r,R)$ with $i_r^*p_r^*=1$. Evaluation on the standard basis identifies the middle sheaf with $R^{\oplus m_r}$, compatibly with restriction. Thus each ordinary dual $(P^r)^\vee$ is finite projective, with the displayed splitting; this is a calculation with finite tuples, including $m_r=0$, rather than a use of projectivity as an object of the global sheaf category. The sheaf-Hom construction is [def-pur-sheaf-hom].

source.place: Tag 08JJ, finite-free/direct-summand calculation in the second paragraph of the proof.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-bounded-free-rhom-model] on the slice with first complex $P$ and second complex $R[0]$. Its hypotheses are satisfied: $P$ is bounded above with each term a displayed summand of a finite free sheaf, and $R[0]$ is bounded below. It represents $H|_U$ by the actual Hom complex $D=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,R[0])$. By [def-pur-hom-complex],
$$D^j=\mathcal Hom_R(P^{-j},R),\qquad d_D^j(\phi)=(-1)^{j+1}\phi\circ d_P^{-j-1}.$$
Hence $D$ is zero outside $[-b,-a]$, its differential squares to zero, and its terms are finite projective by step 3. There is only one nonzero Hom factor in each degree, so there is no infinite-product interchange. These local models prove site-perfectness of $H$ at finite and integral coefficients in [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. The generic ringed-site Hom calculation is what justifies passage from an individual finite-projective term to a bounded complex; the degree-zero tensor-Hom lemma alone would not justify it.

source.place: Tag 08JI (lemma-Rhom-complex-of-direct-summands-finite-free), specialized to the unit in degree zero; Tag 08JJ, strictly perfect dual calculation.

proof.text: At $\Lambda=E$, take the actual bounded local model $P$ of [def-weil-site-perfect-complex] in the raw scalar localization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], using [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization] also on ambient module-derived categories on slices. Set $R_U=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,U}$, and write $T(-)=R\mathcal Hom(-,E_U)$. The rational operation is the integral Hom on objects extended linearly on maps [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The slice-restriction and triangle comparisons in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] therefore rationalize; exact scalar localization [lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated] preserves those triangles. Thus $H|_U=T(P)$. Each term $F=P^r$ has an actual rational splitting $i:F[0]\to E_U^{\oplus m_r}$, $p:E_U^{\oplus m_r}\to F[0]$, $pi=1$. No integral-perfect representative is assumed.

source.place: Rational refinement of the finite-projective dual and canonical-map sentences; extracted from returned step 5.

proof.text: Choose $R_U[0]\to I$ as in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For each term $F=P^r$ apply [lem-sf-rational-term-hom-comparison] on the slice site, with $A=\mathcal O_E$, $t=\varpi_E$, the sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_E$-algebras $R=R_U$, $m=m_r$, and the rational splitting $i:F[0]\to E_U^{\oplus m_r}$, $p:E_U^{\oplus m_r}\to F[0]$, $pi=1$, of step 5; here $E_U^{\oplus m_r}$ is the image of $R_U^{\oplus m_r}[0]$ in the scalar localization, so $i,p$ are exactly the morphisms that lemma assumes. Its conclusions give two facts. First, the chain map $c_F:\mathcal Hom_{R_U}(F,R_U)[0]\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet_{R_U}(F[0],I)$, postcomposition with $R_U[0]\to I$, becomes an isomorphism after scalar localization; its target represents $T(F[0])$. Second, the localized ordinary dual $q(\mathcal Hom_{R_U}(F,R_U)[0])$ is a direct summand of $E_U^{\oplus m_r}$, by actual maps in the raw localization, with no idempotent completion. The splittings are rational; none is assumed to lift integrally, and no integral perfectness of $F$ is used.

source.place: Rational refinement of the finite-projective dual and canonical-map sentences; extracted from returned step 5.

proof.text: To pass from these rational terms to the bounded complex, form the integral module complex $D=\mathcal Hom^\bullet_{R_U}(P,R_U[0])$, with the reversed degrees and signed differential of step 4. Its comparison $D\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet_{R_U}(P,I)$ is induced by $R_U[0]\to I$ in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. We prove it invertible after scalar localization by descending induction on the finite stupid tails $P_{\ge r}$. For $r=b+1$ both complexes are zero. The degreewise split sequence $0\to P_{\ge r+1}\to P_{\ge r}\to P^r[-r]\to0$ gives, after taking Hom, a morphism of short exact sequences by [lem-pc-stupid-tail-hom-short-exact], applied to the map $R_U[0]\to I$. These give a morphism of distinguished triangles by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle], and remain distinguished after exact scalar localization [lem-weil-linear-scalar-localization-triangulated]. The comparison on the single term is $c_{P^r}$ shifted, invertible by step 6; that on the shorter tail is invertible by induction. The third comparison is invertible by [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso]. The connecting maps commute because these are the triangles of that specified morphism of short exact sequences, not arbitrary triangles with the same objects. In the Hom-complex formula [def-pur-hom-complex], the only boundary block is the signed transpose of $d_P^r$: in degree $j=-r-1$ it is $\phi\mapsto(-1)^r\phi d_P^r$ on both sides. This also checks the convention for the connecting map. The induction proves that $D$, rationalized, represents $T(P)=H|_U$. It is bounded in $[-b,-a]$ and its terms are the actual rational finite-projective terms of step 6. Thus it is a model required by [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. This argument uses a finite filtration and the specified Hom comparisons, rather than assuming that an arbitrary exact functor preserves a chosen chain-level totalization.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, bounded termwise-dual argument; Tag 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated). Functorial short-exact-sequence triangles: derived.tex Tag 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor).

proof.text: At $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, [def-weil-site-perfect-complex] supplies a site-perfect representative $K_E$ over some finite coefficient field $E$. By [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible] (3) the common-stage unit is $(\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)_X=(E,E_X)$, independent of the stage, so it may be taken over the same field $E$. By the common-stage definition [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] and the internal-Hom formula in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], with compositum $EE=E$, $H$ is represented over that same field by $R\mathcal Hom(K_E,E_X)$, which is rationally site-perfect by steps 5–7. If a further finite extension is used, [lem-weil-scalar-extension-exact-triangulated] preserves the finite cone constructions, while additivity and functoriality preserve each displayed equation $pi=1$ and finite sum of units. The internal-Hom and unit comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] identify the resulting scalar-extended dual with the dual at the larger field. Thus the models are compatible with the common-stage interpretation, and establish site-perfectness of $H$ at this last coefficient stage as well.

source.place: Local dual-model argument at the common finite coefficient-field stage; main-20261015 prop-sf-dualizable.proof.md and coefficient-stage conventions.

proof.text: Step 1 gives $H\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, and steps 2–8 give its local bounded finite-projective models at the chosen coefficient stage. These are exactly perfectness over $\Lambda_X$ in [def-pod-perfect-complex-on-x]. Since $H$ is the coefficient dual by [def-pod-coefficient-dual-on-x], both conclusions follow. No claim is made that local bounds are automatically uniform on arbitrary sites; the constructible and finite-Tor conclusion was supplied on the actual geometric domain in step 1.

source.place: Final sentence, with constructibility and finite Tor amplitude separately justified at all coefficient stages.

proof_origin.place: Complete local dual-model proof, expanded with Stacks Tags 08JB, 08JI, 08JJ and the already split coefficient-stage constructions. Constructibility uses the existing concrete preservation theorem.
